critique.recommendation_assessment:
Procedure. The rule fixed before the run (sixth clarification) keeps the plans with a fall of 50 % or more in at most 1 path in 20, on paper and at half edge, then takes the highest 12-month median at half edge. That gives F3S (+3,251), not F2S (+3,242). The tie-break (medians within 5 % are tied, then the smallest typical fall of the first 13 weeks) and its 5 % threshold were written after the table was seen. PROTOCOL_V3 says so. The message does not, and picture 7 marks 2 % as 'mon conseil' without saying the declared rule gave 3 %. Honest would have been: '3 % per the rule, a 9 EUR tie; I advise 2 % because it shakes less.'

Noise. I bootstrapped over the 2,000 paths (4,000 resamples, the same resampled paths for every plan). Each 12-month median at half edge is known to about 70 to 100 EUR (s.e.: F2S 76, F3S 68, FS 102; 2 to 3 %). Paired differences:
- F3S - F2S = +9 EUR, s.e. 40, 95 % interval -67 to +90.
- FS - F2S = +116, s.e. 69, interval -5 to +267.
The declared rule itself picks F3S in 65 % of resampled path sets and F2S in 35 %, so its winner is decided by simulation noise. With the tie-break, F2S wins in 100 %.
The faster starts are really ahead on paper, but not by much: at 12 months F3S +196 (s.e. 39) and FS +486 (s.e. 64); at 36 months +466 (215) and +1,078 (267). Without 2024, F3S is +75 (40). At a quarter of paper all starts are within ±60 EUR. If the robot only covers its costs, FS is 206 (72) below F2S.
For 0 to 3 % more gain, F3S triples the chance of a first-quarter fall of 30 % or more (35 % against 12 % of paths) and of a 50 % fall (2.5 % against 0.4 %; worthless rules 21.9 % against 11.5 %). So F2S over F3S is sound in substance.

What is not sound is the framing. The message compares 2 % only with 5 %, which already fails the user's own 50 % limit (23.7 % of paths). It never shows 1 % (F1S), the real alternative for 'losses limited':
- First year: 18 % less, +2,644 against +3,242 (-598, s.e. 57, a real difference); on paper 4,874 against 5,988.
- After 3 years: 4 % less, +16,257 against +16,987.
- A fall of 30 % or more in 3 % of half-edge paths instead of 30 %.

- No 50 % fall in any case, except 0.5 % with worthless rules (F2S: 11.5 %).
- The same loss with worthless rules (-3,564, stop at month 13).
By the user's 'pertes de 10 %, peut-etre 20 %', F1S fits better. By 'very fast at the start', F2S fits better. Both should have been put to him.

1. Months 6-11 make 53-59 % of the typical first-year gain, months 3-5 another 26-29 %, month 12 about 9 %. Months 1-2 make only 5-10 %.

findings.what: F2S is shown as the advice only because of the tie-break added after the run. By the rule fixed before the run, F3S comes first in every draw.
findings.evidence: Over 21 runs (7 seeds x blocks of 4, 8, 16 weeks): F3S first by the declared rule in 21 of 21. The 5 % tie-break picks F2S in 20 of 21; in seed 20261111 with blocks of 4 weeks F2S is at 94.6 % of F3S and the tie-break picks F3S. Across runs F2S's median at 12 months is 94.6-99.7 % of F3S's. A stricter qualification (a fall of 50 % or more in at most 1 % of paths) would pick F2S with no tie-break in 20 of 21 runs.

findings.what: The published gaps '+9 EUR for a 3 % start, +116 for 5 %' at half edge are the smallest of all 21 runs. The typical gaps are about +100 and about +200. The claim that 2 % gives almost the gain of 5 % holds in relative terms.
findings.evidence: At half edge, over 21 runs: F3S minus F2S +9..+172 (about +100 across runs); FS minus F2S +116..+274 (about +160 to +225). The published seed also gives the highest F2S median at 12 months (3,242; range 2,933-3,242). F2S makes 92-97 % of FS's median at half edge and 90-93 % on paper. Path by path at half edge, FS is ahead of F2S in 50-54 % of paths (median difference 0..+18 EUR).

findings.what: The share of paths stopped, and to a lesser degree the 36-month gain, depend strongly on the block length of the draws. The single published figure '8.2 %' is too precise.

Every plan of the ladder moves the same way. F2S's median at 36 months at half edge: 15,700-17,400 for blocks of 4 to 26 weeks, 11,700-12,600 with weeks drawn one by one.
